title: Diagnose unexplained PowerShell Engram authority-child 30-second stall
outcome:
During tm-gldd final-v2 acceptance, the second stacked Engram module run failed once with two byte-identical 30-second authority-child deadline errors. Root cause remains UNEXPLAINED: product process-resume/exit issue versus PowerShell/environment startup stall has not been distinguished. This is not a flaky-test category or a resolved failure.

Evidence: target/tm-gldd-final-v2-module-2.log lines 212-219, 191 passed / 2 failed / 1 ignored, 106.77 s. At that tree src/tests/engram_host_adapter.rs:7647 (engram_mcp_pending_revocation_completes_failed_stop_without_resuming_automatic_work) and :7772 (engram_mcp_pending_revocation_surfaces_shared_codex_stop_interrupt_failure) both reported:
grant clear should defer behind the in-flight Stop: ApiError { message: "Engram capability revocation or runtime cleanup was degraded: the old Engram work-authority grant could not be revoked for one or more runtime targets; a residual MCP child may still mutate until it exits: revocation target 1: Engram authority revocation exceeded 30000 ms; pending behind existing Stop owners: session-1", status: 500, kind: None }

Focused concurrent pair passed 2/2 in 1.06 s. Diagnostic module then passed 193/0/1 in 37.43 s (target/tm-gldd-revocation-diagnostic-module.log); after adding PS/SH phase journals, another diagnostic module passed 193/0/1 in 39.75 s (target/tm-gldd-revocation-instrumented-module.log). Only the latter was phase-instrumented. Read-only process sampling saw no authority process older than 0.5 s. These clean runs do NOT diagnose or resolve the original stall. Three earlier full wrappers also passed, but are not acceptance for the subsequent fixture split.

Safe checks completed: Stop gate parks after releasing the state lock; revocation deadline polls only SharedChild.try_wait after process-tree attach/resume; per-test UUID roots; authority fixture branch precedes control/work branches, stdin=null, tiny argv journal and one stdout record. No evidence yet for a deadlock, cold-start cost, or missed exit publication.

Next occurrence capture: in a separate PowerShell shell at the repo root, run ./src/tests/fixtures/watch-engram-authority.ps1 -OutputPath target/engram-authority-watch.jsonl -Samples 900 -IntervalMs 500 -MinimumAgeSeconds 0.5 while running cargo test --bin termal tests::engram_host_adapter -- --test-threads=4 with complete output retained. Script only reads matching test-fixture authority processes: PID, parent, age, CPU, thread state/wait reason, process count, and the fixture home authority-revoke-phases journal (entered/mode-read/argv-written/exiting). Preserve matching temp-root journal and test log before cleanup; use those to distinguish pre-script startup from script execution or post-exit wait failure. Never inspect/open the live TermAl SQLite database or stop unrelated/live server processes.

Scope decision from Fable #841: two Stop-ordering tests use a native self-exec authority fixture because PowerShell launch is incidental to their subject. Real PowerShell revocation conformance tests and phase journals stay. Keep this bug open independently; the fixture split is not a PowerShell-stall fix. Dedup searched authority revocation, revocation, and PowerShell; tm-8ern, tm-uw7j.7 and tm-46yu concern other revocation semantics, not this stall.
